questions.question: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet.
questions.funFact: Jupiter is more massive than all other planets combined.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks red because of iron oxide on its surface.
questions.funFact: Mars has the tallest volcano in the solar system.

questions.question: Which moon has a thick nitrogen atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Titan, Saturn's moon, has a dense nitrogen-rich atmosphere.
questions.funFact: Titan has lakes and seas of liquid methane and ethane.

questions.question: Which planet rotates on its side?
questions.explanation: Uranus has an axial tilt of about 98 degrees.
questions.funFact: Its seasons last more than 20 Earth years.

questions.question: Which moon is famous for active volcanoes?
questions.explanation: Io is the most volcanically active world known.
questions.funFact: Jupiter's gravity drives Io's intense tidal heating.

questions.question: Which planet has the fastest rotation?
questions.explanation: Jupiter rotates in roughly 10 hours.
questions.funFact: That fast spin helps flatten Jupiter at the poles.

questions.question: Which planet has the hottest surface?
questions.explanation: Venus is hottest because of its runaway greenhouse effect.
questions.funFact: Venus is hotter than Mercury despite being farther from the Sun.

questions.question: What is Pluto classified as today?
questions.explanation: Pluto is classified as a dwarf planet.
questions.funFact: Pluto has a large moon named Charon.

questions.question: Which moon likely has a subsurface ocean?
questions.explanation: Europa has strong evidence for a global ocean under its ice.
questions.funFact: Europa is a major target in the search for life.

questions.question: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
questions.explanation: Neptune is the farthest official planet.
questions.funFact: Neptune was predicted mathematically before it was observed.

questions.question: Who was the first human to walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on July 20, 1969.
questions.funFact: Apollo 11 landed in the Sea of Tranquility.

questions.question: Which spacecraft first landed successfully on Mars?
questions.explanation: Viking 1 landed on Mars in 1976.
questions.funFact: Viking 1 operated for more than six years.

questions.question: Which mission carried the first human into space?
questions.explanation: Yuri Gagarin flew aboard Vostok 1 in 1961.
questions.funFact: The flight completed one orbit of Earth.

questions.question: Which telescope launched in 1990?
questions.explanation: The Hubble Space Telescope launched in 1990.
questions.funFact: Astronauts serviced Hubble several times in orbit.

questions.question: Which mission first flew by Pluto?
questions.explanation: New Horizons flew past Pluto in 2015.
questions.funFact: It revealed Pluto's heart-shaped Tombaugh Regio.

questions.question: Which spacecraft explored Saturn for over a decade?
questions.explanation: Cassini orbited Saturn from 2004 to 2017.
questions.funFact: The Huygens probe landed on Titan.

questions.question: Which rover landed in Jezero Crater?
questions.explanation: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater in 2021.
questions.funFact: It is collecting samples for possible return to Earth.

questions.question: Which mission studies Jupiter today?
questions.explanation: Juno studies Jupiter's atmosphere, magnetic field, and interior.
questions.funFact: Juno follows a highly elliptical polar orbit.

questions.question: Which mission returned comet dust to Earth?
questions.explanation: Stardust returned samples from comet Wild 2.
questions.funFact: Its collector used aerogel to trap particles.

questions.question: Which mission intentionally impacted an asteroid moonlet?
questions.explanation: DART tested asteroid deflection by striking Dimorphos.
questions.funFact: The impact changed Dimorphos's orbital period.

questions.question: What powers main-sequence stars?
questions.explanation: Stars fuse hydrogen into helium in their cores.
questions.funFact: Fusion converts a tiny amount of mass into energy.

questions.question: What is a light-year?
questions.explanation: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year.
questions.funFact: One light-year is about 9.46 trillion kilometers.

questions.question: What is the event horizon?
questions.explanation: It is the boundary beyond which light cannot escape a black hole.
questions.funFact: The first black hole image showed material near an event horizon.

questions.question: What is redshift often used to measure?
questions.explanation: Redshift can show that distant galaxies are receding.
questions.funFact: Greater redshift often means greater cosmic distance.

questions.question: What is a neutron star?
questions.explanation: A neutron star is the ultra-dense remnant of a massive star.
questions.funFact: A spoonful of neutron star matter would be enormously massive.

questions.question: What does the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram compare?
questions.explanation: The H-R diagram plots stellar luminosity against temperature.
questions.funFact: It reveals main sequence stars, giants, and white dwarfs.

questions.question: What is dark matter mainly inferred from?
questions.explanation: Dark matter is inferred from gravitational effects.
questions.funFact: It does not emit ordinary light.

questions.question: What is a supernova?
questions.explanation: A supernova is a powerful stellar explosion.
questions.funFact: Supernovae help create and spread heavy elements.

questions.question: What is the cosmic microwave background?
questions.explanation: It is ancient radiation left from the early hot universe.
questions.funFact: It is one of the strongest pieces of evidence for the Big Bang model.

questions.question: What causes tides on Earth most strongly?
questions.explanation: The Moon's gravity is the main driver of tides.
questions.funFact: The Sun also contributes to tides.

questions.question: What does a rocket nozzle do?
questions.explanation: A nozzle accelerates hot exhaust gases.
questions.funFact: Nozzle shape depends on pressure and mission environment.

questions.question: What is specific impulse?
questions.explanation: Specific impulse measures propulsion efficiency.
questions.funFact: Higher Isp means more impulse per unit propellant.

questions.question: What does GPS rely on?
questions.explanation: GPS satellites use precise atomic clocks.
questions.funFact: Relativity corrections are needed for GPS accuracy.

questions.question: What is aerobraking?
options: Using atmosphere to slow a spacecraft
questions.explanation: Aerobraking reduces orbital energy using atmospheric drag.
questions.funFact: It can save a large amount of propellant.

questions.question: What does JWST mainly observe?
questions.explanation: JWST is optimized for infrared astronomy.
questions.funFact: Its sunshield is about the size of a tennis court.

questions.question: What is SGP4 used for?
questions.explanation: SGP4 propagates satellite positions from TLE data.
questions.funFact: It is widely used for Earth-orbiting satellite tracking.

questions.question: What is a heat shield for?
questions.explanation: A heat shield protects spacecraft during atmospheric reentry.
questions.funFact: Some heat shields ablate, carrying heat away as material burns off.

questions.question: What is an ion engine known for?
questions.explanation: Ion engines are efficient but produce low thrust.
questions.funFact: They can operate for very long durations.

questions.question: What is a TLE?
questions.explanation: A TLE stores orbital data in two formatted lines.
questions.funFact: TLEs are commonly used to track satellites.

questions.question: What does a reaction wheel control?
questions.explanation: Reaction wheels help rotate and point spacecraft.
questions.funFact: They exchange angular momentum with the spacecraft body.

questions.question: Who was the first woman in space?
questions.explanation: Valentina Tereshkova flew in 1963.
questions.funFact: She orbited Earth 48 times.

questions.question: Who was the first American woman in space?
questions.explanation: Sally Ride flew aboard Challenger in 1983.
questions.funFact: She was also a physicist.

questions.question: Who was the first African American woman in space?
questions.explanation: Mae Jemison flew on Space Shuttle Endeavour in 1992.
questions.funFact: She is also a physician and engineer.

questions.question: Who stayed in orbit while Armstrong and Aldrin walked on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Michael Collins piloted the Apollo 11 command module.
questions.funFact: He orbited the Moon alone during the landing.

questions.question: Who was the first American to orbit Earth?
questions.explanation: John Glenn orbited Earth in 1962.
questions.funFact: He later returned to space at age 77.

questions.question: Who commanded Apollo 13?
questions.explanation: Jim Lovell commanded Apollo 13.
questions.funFact: Apollo 13 survived a major oxygen tank failure.

questions.question: Who was the first person to perform a spacewalk?
questions.explanation: Alexei Leonov performed the first EVA in 1965.
questions.funFact: His suit expanded, making reentry into the capsule difficult.

questions.question: Who was the first Canadian commander of the ISS?
questions.explanation: Chris Hadfield commanded the ISS in 2013.
questions.funFact: He became famous for music and education from orbit.

questions.question: Who holds major cumulative time-in-space records among NASA astronauts?
questions.explanation: Peggy Whitson has held major NASA duration records.
questions.funFact: She has commanded the ISS more than once.

questions.question: Who was the last person to walk on the Moon in Apollo?
questions.explanation: Gene Cernan was the last person on the lunar surface during Apollo 17.
questions.funFact: Apollo 17 launched in December 1972.

questions.question: What is NASA's Artemis program focused on?
questions.explanation: Artemis focuses on lunar exploration and preparation for Mars.
questions.funFact: Artemis includes the Space Launch System and Orion spacecraft.

questions.question: What is SpaceX Starship designed to be?
questions.explanation: Starship is intended as a reusable heavy-lift launch system.
questions.funFact: It is central to several lunar and Mars ambitions.

questions.question: What is the Lunar Gateway?
questions.explanation: Gateway is planned as a station in lunar orbit.
questions.funFact: It will support Artemis missions.

questions.question: What does CLPS stand for?
questions.explanation: CLPS delivers science and technology payloads to the Moon.
questions.funFact: It uses commercial lunar landers.

questions.question: What is the ISS primarily used for?
questions.explanation: The ISS supports research in microgravity.
questions.funFact: Experiments cover biology, physics, medicine, and technology.

questions.question: What does ESA stand for?
questions.explanation: ESA is the European Space Agency.
questions.funFact: ESA works with NASA and other partners on many missions.

questions.question: What is the main goal of planetary defense missions?
questions.explanation: Planetary defense tracks and studies potentially hazardous objects.
questions.funFact: DART was a planetary defense demonstration.

questions.question: What is OSIRIS-REx famous for?
questions.explanation: OSIRIS-REx returned samples from asteroid Bennu.
questions.funFact: Its sample capsule landed in Utah.

questions.question: What does a cubesat usually mean?
questions.explanation: CubeSats are small satellites built to standard unit sizes.
questions.funFact: They make space missions more accessible.

questions.question: What is commercial crew?
options: Private spacecraft carrying astronauts for NASA
questions.explanation: Commercial Crew uses private spacecraft to transport astronauts.
questions.funFact: Crew Dragon has flown astronauts to the ISS.
